comment: Topic-specific management steps (NICE-based). Key = lowercase keyword match in tool title. First match wins.

options.label: Scalp Psoriasis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Potent corticosteroid scalp application (e.g. Betcap or Betnovate) once daily for 4 weeks.
2. Scaling: Use coal tar shampoo (e.g. Alphosyl) or salicylic acid preparation to remove thick scale before steroid.
3. Review: Review at 4 weeks. NICE CG153.

options.label: Seborrhoeic Dermatitis (Scalp)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Medicated Shampoo: Ketoconazole 2% (Nizoral) or coal tar based (Alphosyl/Capasal) twice weekly for 2-4 weeks.
2. Inflammation: If severe itch/redness, use moderate potency topical steroid application (e.g. Eumovate scalp) for up to 4 weeks.
3. Maintenance: Use medicated shampoo once weekly/fortnightly as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Chronic Plaque Psoriasis (Skin)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Potent corticosteroid + Vitamin D analogue (e.g. Enstilar foam or Dovobet gel) once daily for up to 4 weeks.
2. Review: Review at 4 weeks. If not controlled, consider Vitamin D analogue bd or potent steroid bd.
3. Emollients: Use regularly to reduce scaling.
4. Scalp: See separate scalp management if involved. NICE CG153.

options.label: Scalp Psoriasis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Potent corticosteroid scalp application (e.g. Betcap or Betnovate) once daily for 4 weeks.
2. Scaling: Use coal tar shampoo (e.g. Alphosyl) or salicylic acid preparation to remove thick scale before steroid.
3. Review: Review at 4 weeks. NICE CG153.

options.label: Face, Flexures, or Genitals
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Mild or moderate potency corticosteroid (e.g. Hydrocortisone 1% or Eumovate) used for a maximum of 2 weeks.
2. Monitoring: High risk of skin atrophy in these areas. NICE CG153.

options.label: Referral Criteria
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Erythrodermic or generalized pustular psoriasis (Same day).
2. Routine: Diagnostic uncertainty, extensive disease (>10% BSA), or failure of topical therapy after 2-3 months. NICE CG153.

options.label: Standard Skin Care Plan
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Skincare: Use soap substitutes (emollients) for washing. Avoid harsh soaps and detergents.
2. Emollients: Apply liberal amounts of emollient cream/ointment frequently to maintain skin barrier.
3. Triggers: Identify and avoid potential irritants or allergens.
4. Safety-net: Return if signs of infection (weeping, crusting, fever) or no improvement in 2 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Acute Paronychia (Bacterial)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Conservative: Warm saline soaks 3-4 times daily.
2. Topical: If minor, use topical antiseptic (Fucidin) or mupirocin.
3. Oral: If severe or cellulitis present, start flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 7 days (clarithromycin if penicillin-allergic).
4. Drainage: If abscess present, perform incision and drainage.
5. Safety-net: Return if fever, spreading redness, or no change in 48h. NICE CKS.

options.label: Chronic Paronychia (>6 weeks)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Protection: Avoid moisture/irritants; use cotton-lined gloves for wet work.
2. Topical: Use topical steroid (e.g. hydrocortisone / Betnovate) and/or topical antifungal (clotrimazole).
3. Hygiene: Keep area dry; avoid nail-biting.
4. Review: Primary care review in 4-6 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Conservative / Self-care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Soak foot: Warm salty water (10-15 mins, 3-4x daily).
2. Lifting nail: Gently lift nail edge with a clean wisp (if comfortable).
3. Footwear: Wear wide, comfortable shoes or sandals.
4. Nail care: Cut nails straight across, not too short at corners. NICE CKS.

options.label: Infected nail fold
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Check for spreading cellulitis or systemic symptoms.
2. Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 7 days (or clarithromycin).
3. Review: Review in 48-72h. If not improving, consider incision/drainage or specialist referral. NICE CKS.

options.label: Surgical referral (Podiatry)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Persistent pain, recurrent infection, or failure of conservative measures.
2. Procedure: Partial or total nail avulsion with phenolisation.
3. Referral: Refer to local podiatry or minor surgery clinic. NICE CKS.

options.label: General / Skin Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triggers: Avoid heat, spicy food, alcohol, and UV exposure.
2. Sunscreen: Use broad-spectrum high SPF daily.
3. Skincare: Use gentle soap-free cleansers; avoid topical steroids.
4. Eye check: Check for gritty eyes/redness (ocular rosacea). NICE CKS.

options.label: Topical treatment (Papulopustular)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line (Mild): Topical ivermectin (Soolantra) once daily, OR metronidazole 0.75% gel/cream bd.
2. Alternative: Topical azelaic acid 15% gel bd.
3. Duration: Trial for 8-12 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Oral treatment (Moderate/Severe)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: More severe disease or failure of topical therapy.
2. Medication: Oxytetracycline 500mg bd, OR Doxycycline 100mg od (or 40mg modified-release).
3. Course: 6-12 weeks initially. NICE CKS.

options.label: First Aid (Acute)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Position: Lean forward, do not swallow blood.
2. Compression: Firmly pinch lower soft part of nose for 10-15 mins without release.
3. Warnings: If bleeding >15 mins or severe, attend A&E. NICE CKS.

options.label: Primary Care Cautery
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identification: Identify bleeding point (usually Little's area on septum).
2. Technique: Anesthetize then apply Silver Nitrate (75%) for 1-5 seconds.
3. Post-care: Apply Naseptin (check peanut/soy allergy) or petroleum jelly bd for 10 days. NICE CKS.

options.label: Recurrent / Prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Ointment: Apply antiseptic cream (Naseptin) to nostrils bd for 10 days to reduce crusting/infection.
2. Habits: Avoid nose-picking, hot baths, and heavy lifting for 24h after a bleed.
3. Review meds: Review use of anticoagulants/antiplatelets if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Localised (Non-bullous)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Hydrogen peroxide 1% cream (Crystacide) for 5 days.
2. Alternative: Topical fusidic acid 2% tds for 5 days (if peroxide unsuitable).
3. Hygiene: Crusts can be gently soaked off with warm water. NICE CKS.

options.label: Widespread or Bullous
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Oral Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 5 days (clarithromycin if allergic).
2. Bullous: Always use oral antibiotics as it is usually staphylococcal.
3. Hygiene: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching. NICE CKS.

options.label: Exclusion / Contagion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. School/Work: Exclude until lesions are crusted and healed, OR 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
2. Recurrence: Consider nasal swab (MRSA?) and skin de-colonization. NICE CKS.

options.label: Scalp Psoriasis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Potent corticosteroid scalp application (e.g. Betcap or Betnovate) once daily for 4 weeks.
2. Scaling: Use coal tar shampoo (e.g. Alphosyl) or salicylic acid preparation to remove thick scale before steroid.
3. Review: Review at 4 weeks. NICE CG153.

options.label: Seborrhoeic Dermatitis (Scalp)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Medicated Shampoo: Ketoconazole 2% (Nizoral) or coal tar based (Alphosyl/Capasal) twice weekly for 2-4 weeks.
2. Inflammation: If severe itch/redness, use moderate potency topical steroid application (e.g. Eumovate scalp) for up to 4 weeks.
3. Maintenance: Use medicated shampoo once weekly/fortnightly as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tinea Capitis (Scalp Ringworm)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: All suspected tinea capitis should be referred to dermatology for confirmation (scalp scrapings/hair pluck) and systemic treatment.
2. Caution: Topical treatment is not effective for scalp ringworm. NICE CKS.

options.label: Acute Paronychia (Bacterial)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Conservative: Warm saline soaks 3-4 times daily.
2. Topical: If minor, use topical antiseptic (Fucidin) or mupirocin.
3. Oral: If severe or cellulitis present, start flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 7 days (clarithromycin if penicillin-allergic).
4. Drainage: If abscess present, perform incision and drainage.
5. Safety-net: Return if fever, spreading redness, or no change in 48h. NICE CKS.

options.label: Chronic Paronychia (>6 weeks)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Protection: Avoid moisture/irritants; use cotton-lined gloves for wet work.
2. Topical: Use topical steroid (e.g. hydrocortisone / Betnovate) and/or topical antifungal (clotrimazole).
3. Hygiene: Keep area dry; avoid nail-biting.
4. Review: Primary care review in 4-6 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Scalp (Adult)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Medicated Shampoo: Ketoconazole 2% (Nizoral) or coal tar based (Alphosyl/Capasal) twice weekly for 2-4 weeks.
2. Inflammation: If severe itch/redness, use moderate potency topical steroid application (e.g. Eumovate scalp) for up to 4 weeks.
3. Maintenance: Use medicated shampoo once weekly/fortnightly as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Face and Body
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antifungal: Topical ketoconazole 2% cream or miconazole once or twice daily for 2-4 weeks.
2. Steroid: If inflamed, use mild topical steroid (e.g. Hydrocortisone 1%) for short course (max 2 weeks).
3. Hygiene: Use soap substitute; avoid greasy ointments. NICE CKS.

options.label: Cradle Cap (Infant)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Soften scale: Use baby oil, olive oil, or coconut oil to soften crusts overnight.
2. Brush: Gently brush off scale with a soft brush or fine-toothed comb.
3. Wash: Use baby shampoo to wash hair. Safety-net: Return if spreading to face/flexures or looking infected. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mild / Single lesion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical: Diclofenac 3% gel (Solaraze) twice daily for 60-90 days.
2. Cryotherapy: Consider if single, well-defined lesion.
3. Sun Protection: High SPF broad-spectrum sunscreen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate / Field change (>5 lesions)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical First-line: Fluorouracil 5% cream (Efudix) once daily for 3-4 weeks. Warn patient of expected inflammatory 'crusting' reaction.
2. Alternative: Imiquimod 5% cream (Aldara) 3 times weekly for 4 weeks (review then repeat as needed).
3. Warning: If any lesion is painful, ulcerated, or growing, suspect SCC and refer 2WW. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tinea Corporis / Cruris / Pedis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical: Terbinafine 1% cream once daily for 1 week, OR Clotrimazole 1% cream twice daily for 2-4 weeks.
2. Duration: Continue for 1 week after clinical resolution.
3. Hygiene: Keep area clean/dry; avoid sharing towels. NICE CKS.

options.label: Pityriasis Versicolor
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Ketoconazole 2% shampoo (Nizoral) used as body wash once daily for 5 days.
2. Alternative: Selenium sulfide (Selsun) body wash.
3. Note: Pigmentation changes may take months to resolve after treatment. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mild (Single nail / Distal)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostics: Confirm with nail clippings (microscopy/culture) before oral treatment.
2. Topical: Amorolfine 5% nail lacquer once weekly for 6 (fingers) to 12 (toes) months.
3. Advice: Keep nails short; use separate clippers for infected nail. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate/Severe (Multiple nails / Proximal)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostics: Mandatory nail clipping confirmation.
2. Oral: Terbinafine 250mg once daily (6 weeks for fingers, 3-6 months for toes).
3. Monitoring: Baseline LFTs if high risk or long course. NICE CKS.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

options.label: Regular, no red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
History: triggers, duration. Check FBC, U&E, TFT. Consider 24h tape if intermittent. Reassure if benign; treat anxiety if relevant. NICE NG196.

options.label: Irregular or suspected AF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
ECG (or rhythm strip). If AF: assess stroke risk (CHA2DS2-Vasc), bleeding (HAS-BLED), rate/rhythm control. Anticoagulate per NICE NG196. Refer if haemodynamically unstable or first confirmed AF for consideration of rhythm control.

options.label: Red flags (syncope, chest pain, SOB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
ECG urgently. Consider same-day referral or ambulance if syncope, chest pain, or severe SOB. Exclude VT, heart block, PE. NICE NG196.

options.label: Suspected COPD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.7). Staging by FEV1%. Assess breathlessness (MRC), exacerbations. Exclude asthma. NICE NG115.

options.label: Stable COPD – step-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Step 1: SABA reliever as needed (e.g. Salbutamol / Ventolin). Step 2: add a LAMA (e.g. Tiotropium / Spiriva) or a LABA (e.g. Salmeterol / Serevent). Step 3: Dual therapy (LAMA+LABA e.g. Anoro / Spiolto). Step 4: Triple therapy (LABA+LAMA+ICS e.g. Trelegy / Trimbow) if eosinophils ≥0.3 or ≥2 exacerbations/year. Offer pulmonary rehab. NICE NG115.

options.label: Acute exacerbation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Prednisolone 30 mg 7–14 days. Antibiotic if purulent sputum: doxycycline or amoxicillin (or clarithromycin). Increase bronchodilators. Consider hospital if severe. NICE NG115.

options.label: Step 1 – SABA only
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Intermittent asthma: SABA reliever as needed (e.g. Salbutamol / Ventolin). If using SABA ≥3/week or symptoms ≥3/week: add a low-dose ICS preventer (e.g. Clenil / Beclometasone) (step 2). NICE NG80.

options.label: Step 2–3 – ICS ± LABA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Step 2: low-dose ICS (e.g. Clenil). Step 3: add a LABA (e.g. Salmeterol) alongside ICS (e.g. Seretide combination). If good control on low ICS+LABA, consider trial of LABA withdrawal. NICE NG80.

options.label: Step 4–5 – add-on
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Step 4: increase ICS dose or change to MART (Maintenance and Reliever Therapy e.g. Fostair / Symbicort) or add LTRA (Montelukast). Step 5: add prednisolone or refer for biologicals. Check technique and adherence. NICE NG80.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

options.label: Mild
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Watchful waiting, active monitoring, or psychological intervention (CBT, exercise). Do not offer antidepressant as first-line. NICE NG222.

options.label: Moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
SSRI (e.g. sertraline) or psychological intervention. Review at 2 weeks; continue 6 months after remission. NICE NG222.

options.label: Severe or treatment-resistant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Combination antidepressant + high-intensity psychological therapy. Consider referral. Risk assess; consider crisis if suicidal. NICE NG222.

options.label: Sertraline (1st-line if CVD risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Starting Dose: 50mg OD.
2. Info: Warn about 'initial worsening' of anxiety (first 2 weeks) and GI side effects. NICE NG222.

options.label: Fluoxetine (1st-line for youth/child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Only SSRI licensed for <18s (under specialist guidance). NICE NG222.

options.label: Citalopram (Watch QTc)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Max dose 20mg if age >65 or hepatic impairment (risk of QTc prolongation). NICE NG222.

options.label: Initial Follow-up (Age <25 or high risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review in 1 week to check for suicidal ideation or agitation. NICE NG222.

options.label: Standard Follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review in 2-4 weeks. Assess efficacy and side effects. NICE NG222.

options.label: Woman (Non-pregnant)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg MR bd (if eGFR ≥45) or Trimethoprim 200mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: Man
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Always send MSU. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg MR bd.
2. Duration: 7 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: Pregnant Woman
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Always send MSU. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg (avoid at term) or Cefalexin.
2. Duration: 7 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: First-line Advice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Eat regular meals; drink ≥ 8 cups fluid (non-caffeinated).
2. Limit high-fibre bread/cereals. Reduce resistant starch.
3. Trial low-FODMAP only after specialist dietitian advice. NICE NG61.

options.label: Pain / Cramping
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antispasmodics (e.g. Mebeverine 135mg tds or Buscopan 10mg-20mg qds). NICE NG61.

options.label: Constipation (IBS-C)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bulk-forming laxatives (e.g. Ispaghula / Fybogel). Avoid lactulose. NICE NG61.

options.label: Diarrhoea (IBS-D)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Loperamide 2mg-4mg as needed. NICE NG61.

options.label: Second-line (Refractory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Tricyclic Antidepressant (e.g. Amitriptyline 10mg nocte) as analgesic. NICE NG61.

options.label: No red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Advise stay active; paracetamol + NSAID short-term. Consider manual therapy. Do not offer imaging. Review at 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Red flags (cauda equina, fracture, infection)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Cauda equina: emergency referral. Consider fracture if trauma/steroids; infection if fever. MRI if nerve root compression suspected for surgical option. NICE NG59.

options.label: Acute attack
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
NSAID (e.g. naproxen) + PPI, or colchicine 500 mcg bd–qd (max 6 mg per attack), or prednisolone 30 mg 3–5 days. Start within 24 h. NICE NG219.

options.label: Urate-lowering (recurrent or tophi)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Allopurinol 100 mg daily, titrate to target sUA <300 µmol/L. Prophylaxis: colchicine or NSAID for first 6 months. NICE NG219.

options.label: Suspected (Raised NT-proBNP)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NT-proBNP > 2000: Urgent Specialist Assessment / Echo (within 2 weeks).
2. NT-proBNP 400-2000: Routine Specialist Assessment / Echo (within 6 weeks).
3. NT-proBNP < 400: Heart Failure unlikely. NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFrEF (EF ≤ 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Start 'Four Pillars' as soon as tolerated.
2. Review symptoms (NYHA class). NICE NG106.

options.label: Confirmed HFpEF (EF > 40%)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Manage comorbidities (Hypertension, AF, Diabetes).
2. Diuretics for fluid overload. NICE NG106.

options.label: First-line: ACEi/ARB + Beta Blocker
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titrate up every 2 weeks unless limited by BP/Pulse.
2. ACEi (e.g. Ramipril) -> Switch to ARNI (Entresto) if symptoms persist. NICE NG106.

options.label: MRA (Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Eplerenone or Spironolactone. Monitor U&E (K+) closely. NICE NG106.

options.label: SGLT2 Inhibitor
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dapagliflozin or Empagliflozin 10mg OD. Does not require titration. NICE NG106.

options.label: G1-G3 (eGFR ≥ 30)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Monitor: Annual eGFR and ACR.
2. Target: BP < 140/90 (or < 130/80 if ACR ≥ 70). NICE NG203.

options.label: G4-G5 (eGFR < 30)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Specialist referral to Nephrology.
2. Prepare for renal replacement therapy discussions. NICE NG203.

options.label: Albuminuria (ACR ≥ 3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin 10mg) is indicated to reduce progression risk. NICE NG203.

options.label: Proteinuria (ACR ≥ 30)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (titrate to maximum tolerated dose). NICE NG203.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Mild Eczema
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emollients: Apply liberally and frequently (250g-500g per week). Use even when skin is clear.
2. Flare: Mild potency topical steroid (e.g. Hydrocortisone 1%) once or twice daily for up to 2 weeks.
3. Hygiene: Use emollient as soap substitute. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate Eczema
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Flare: Moderate potency topical steroid (e.g. Eumovate / Betnovate-RD) once or twice daily for up to 2 weeks.
2. Maintenance: Consider 'weekend' use of steroid on common flare areas if frequent recurrences.
3. Antihistamine: Non-sedating (e.g. Cetirizine) for itch if needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Severe Eczema
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Flare: Potent topical steroid (e.g. Betnovate / Elocon) once or twice daily for up to 2 weeks. Do not use potent steroids on face/flexures.
2. Infection: Suspect if weeping, crusting, or failing to improve. Swab and start Flucloxacillin.
3. Referral: Failure of potent steroids or impact on sleep/quality of life. NICE CKS.

options.label: Scalp Involvement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Shampoo: Coal tar based shampoo (Capasal) or Ketoconazole (Nizoral) if seborrhoeic overlap.
2. Steroid: Moderate or potent steroid scalp application/lotion for up to 4 weeks. NICE CKS.

options.label: Primary prevention, QRISK3 ≥10%
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Offer atorvastatin 20 mg (or simvastatin 40 mg if atorvastatin not tolerated). Discuss lifestyle. Recheck lipids in 3 months. NICE NG238.

options.label: Primary prevention, high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider higher intensity (atorvastatin 80 mg) if QRISK3 ≥10% and lifestyle addressed. NICE NG238.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). Aim LDL reduction >40%. Add ezetimibe if not at target. NICE NG238.

options.label: Score 0–1 (no antibiotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Safety-net: if worsening or no improvement in 1 week, re-assess. NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 2–3
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Back-up or immediate antibiotic: phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg qds 5–10 days (or clarithromycin if penicillin allergic). NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 4–5
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Immediate antibiotic. Consider throat swab. Penicillin 10 days. NICE NG84.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: Likely viral (<10 days)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Advise if no improvement by 10 days or worsening, re-assess. NICE NG79.

options.label: Persistent or severe
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider phenoxymethylpenicillin or co-amoxiclav 7 days if no improvement after 10 days or severe. NICE NG79.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Increase fibre, fluids, activity. Consider bulk-forming (e.g. ispaghula). NICE NG99.

options.label: Osmotic / stimulant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Osmotic: macrogol. Stimulant: senna or bisacodyl short-term. Avoid long-term stimulant. NICE NG99.

options.label: Uninvestigated Dyspepsia / GORD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle: Weight loss, stop smoking, avoid late meals/triggers.
2. Medication: PPI (e.g. Omeprazole 20mg or Lansoprazole 30mg) for 4 weeks.
3. H. pylori: Test (stool/breath) and treat if positive. NICE CG184.

options.label: Refractory Symptoms
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review: Check compliance and timing (30-60m before food).
2. Dose: Increase PPI to twice daily or switch PPI.
3. Referral: Consider referral for endoscopy if symptoms persist despite high-dose PPI. NICE CG184.

options.label: Urgent Referral (2WW)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dysphagia: Any age with difficulty swallowing.
2. Weight Loss: Age ≥55 with weight loss AND (dyspepsia OR reflux).
3. Action: Refer via 2WW pathway. NICE NG12.

options.label: Acute migraine
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Triptan + NSAID (or paracetamol). Anti-emetic if nausea. Avoid opiates. NICE NG150.

options.label: Prophylaxis (≥8 days/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Propranolol or topiramate. Consider referral if not controlled. NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: No uterus – oestrogen only
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen only (patch/gel preferred for VTE risk). Review annually. NICE NG23.

options.label: With uterus – combined
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen + cyclical or continuous progestogen. Sequential if perimenopausal; continuous if postmenopausal. NICE NG23.

options.label: Contraindications / alternatives
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contraindications: breast cancer, VTE, stroke. Consider non-hormonal (clonidine, CBT) or topical oestrogen for urogenital. NICE NG23.

options.label: G3a (eGFR 45–59)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Confirm with repeat; address CV risk, BP (target <130/80 if diabetic/proteinuric). Avoid nephrotoxics. NICE NG203.

options.label: G3b–4 (eGFR 15–44)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Monitor 6–12 monthly. Anaemia, bone, K+. Refer if eGFR <30 or rapid decline. Consider SGLT2i if T2DM. NICE NG203.

options.label: G5 (eGFR <15)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer nephrology. Plan for RRT. Manage complications. NICE NG203.

options.label: Mild (comedones)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Topical: adapalene 0.1% or benzoyl peroxide 5% OD. If inadequate after 12 weeks add topical antibiotic (e.g. clindamycin). NICE NG198.

options.label: Moderate (inflammatory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Fixed combination: adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, or topical abx + benzoyl peroxide. If inadequate: oral doxycycline 100 mg OD 12 weeks (or lymecycline). NICE NG198.

options.label: Severe or scarring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology for oral isotretinoin. Exclude pregnancy; contraception. Do not offer oral antibiotic long-term as monotherapy. NICE NG198.

options.label: Mild (no systemic features)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oral flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 7 days (or clarithromycin 500 mg bd if penicillin allergic). Elevate limb. Review at 48 h. NICE NG141.

options.label: Moderate (fever, spreading)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oral co-amoxiclav 500/125 mg tds 7 days, or flucloxacillin + phenoxymethylpenicillin. Consider IV if not improving. NICE NG141.

options.label: Severe / orbital / facial
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Admit for IV benzylpenicillin or flucloxacillin. 2WW not appropriate; emergency assessment. NICE NG141.

options.label: Stroke prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 (men) or ≥3 (women): offer anticoagulation. DOAC preferred (apixaban 5 mg bd, rivaroxaban 20 mg OD, edoxaban, dabigatran). Warfarin if DOAC unsuitable. HAS-BLED for bleeding risk. NICE NG196.

options.label: Rate control
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Beta-blocker (bisoprolol) or rate-limiting CCB (diltiazem). Digoxin if sedentary. Target resting HR <110 (or <80 if symptomatic). NICE NG196.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer cardiology: first confirmed AF, for rhythm control or ablation; young; haemodynamically unstable. Emergency if severe haemodynamic compromise. NICE NG196.

options.label: Wells score – likely DVT
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
D-dimer if Wells 1–2; if positive or Wells ≥3 do proximal leg USS. If DVT confirmed: anticoagulate. NICE NG158.

options.label: Confirmed DVT – anticoagulation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
DOAC (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban) or warfarin. Apixaban 10 mg bd 7 days then 5 mg bd. Minimum 3 months; extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk. NICE NG158.

options.label: Suspected PE
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Wells PE; D-dimer (if low clinical probability); if positive CTPA. Treat as per NG158. Admit if haemodynamically unstable.

options.label: CURB65 0–1 (home)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oral amoxicillin 500 mg tds 5 days (or doxycycline 200 mg stat then 100 mg OD if penicillin allergic). Safety-net. NICE NG138.

options.label: CURB65 2
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider hospital; if home: oral amoxicillin 1 g tds or co-amoxiclav. Consider co-amoxiclav if atypical suspected. NICE NG138.

options.label: CURB65 ≥3
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Admit. IV co-amoxiclav or benzylpenicillin + clarithromycin. NICE NG138.

options.label: Iron deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD or bd (or ferrous fumarate). Recheck Hb in 2–4 weeks. Continue 3 months after normal. If not responding: check compliance, consider malabsorption, 2WW if red flags. NICE NG24.

options.label: B12 deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM 3× per week 2 weeks then 1 mg every 3 months (or oral if mild and compliant). Check folate. NICE NG241.

options.label: Macrocytic (B12/folate)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check B12 and folate. Treat as above. If both normal consider alcohol, hypothyroid, MDS – consider referral. NICE NG24.

options.label: Suspected new RA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
2WW rheumatology if persistent synovitis. Check RF, anti-CCP, CRP, FBC, U&E, LFT. Start DMARD within 3 months. NICE NG100.

options.label: DMARD choice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
First-line: methotrexate 15 mg weekly (folic acid 5 mg weekly). Add sulfasalazine or hydroxychloroquine if MTX incomplete. Monitor FBC, LFT, creatinine. NICE NG100.

options.label: Acute flare
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Short-term prednisolone (e.g. 15 mg OD reducing over 3 weeks). Do not use long-term steroid without DMARD. NICE NG100.

options.label: Core treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Exercise, weight loss if overweight. Paracetamol prn. Topical NSAID (e.g. ibuprofen gel) for knee/hand. NICE NG226.

options.label: Oral NSAID
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oral NSAID at lowest dose (e.g. ibuprofen 400 mg tds) + PPI. Use short-term. Avoid if CKD, high CV risk. Consider topical first for knee. NICE NG226.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider referral for joint replacement if severe impact despite non-surgical treatment. NICE NG226.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Diet: fibre, low FODMAP trial. Avoid trigger foods. Antispasmodic (e.g. mebeverine 135 mg tds or hyoscine). NICE NG61.

options.label: IBS-D
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Loperamide prn. Consider trial of low-dose amitriptyline (10 mg) if refractory. NICE NG61.

options.label: IBS-C
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Linaclotide 290 mcg OD if inadequate response to laxatives. NICE NG61.

options.label: Diagnosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
IgA TTG + total IgA. If positive refer for duodenal biopsy. Do not start gluten-free diet before biopsy. NICE NG20.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lifelong gluten-free diet. Dietitian referral. Annual review: Hb, B12, folate, ferritin, TFT, bone. NICE NG20.

options.label: Refractory
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer gastroenterology if symptoms persist despite strict GFD. Exclude lymphoma. NICE NG20.

options.label: Uncomplicated
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
High-fibre diet. Avoid routine antibiotics. Bulk-forming laxative if constipation. NICE NG147.

options.label: Acute diverticulitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Mild: oral co-amoxiclav or ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 5–7 days. Clear fluids if severe. Admit if systemically unwell, peritonism, or not improving. NICE NG147.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer if recurrent attacks, complications (abscess, fistula, stricture), or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG147.

options.label: Fever + non-blanching rash
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Treat as meningococcal disease until proved otherwise. Immediate parenteral antibiotic (ceftriaxone or benzylpenicillin). Emergency admission. NICE NG51.

options.label: No fever, well child
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider ITP, HSP. FBC, clotting. Refer paediatrics if unwell or platelets <20. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected melanoma
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
2WW dermatology. Do not excise in primary care. ABCDE criteria; any changing mole or ulcerated lesion. NICE NG14.

options.label: Suspected BCC
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Routine referral or minor surgery if appropriate. NICE NG12.

options.label: Suspected SCC
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
2WW. Urgent if high risk (size, site, immunosuppression). NICE NG12.

options.label: Standard
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Permethrin 5% cream: apply to whole body (neck down), leave 8–12 h, repeat after 7 days. Treat all household contacts. Wash bedding. CKS Scabies.

options.label: Crusted
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology. Ivermectin (unlicensed) or permethrin under supervision. CKS Scabies.

options.label: Acute TIA (ABCD2 ≥4 or crescendo)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Same-day specialist assessment. Aspirin 300 mg immediately then 75 mg OD. NICE NG128.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Antiplatelet: clopidogrel 75 mg OD (or aspirin + dipyridamole). BP and lipid targets. Consider anticoagulation if AF. NICE NG128.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
All TIAs: urgent referral for investigation (imaging, carotid). NICE NG128.

options.label: First seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer neurologist (2WW). Do not drive until assessed. EEG and MRI. NICE NG217.

options.label: Drug choice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
First-line: levetiracetam, lamotrigine, or carbamazepine (depending on seizure type). Monotherapy; titrate. NICE NG217.

options.label: Pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
High-dose folic acid 5 mg. Review drugs (valproate avoid). Specialist advice. NICE NG217.

options.label: Visible haematuria (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer urology 2WW. Exclude UTI; if UTI treat and repeat urine. NICE NG12.

options.label: Non-visible (≥45)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
FBC, U&E, eGFR. Refer 2WW if eGFR <60 or other concern. Otherwise routine referral for cystoscopy/imaging. NICE NG12.

options.label: Medical management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Alpha-blocker (tamsulosin 400 mcg OD) for flow. 5-alpha reductase inhibitor (finasteride 5 mg) if enlarged prostate. Combination if both. NICE NG97.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer urology: retention, recurrent UTI, stones, renal impairment, failed medical treatment, or suspected cancer. NICE NG97.

options.label: NRT
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Nicotine patch + short-acting (gum/lozenge) for cravings. 8–12 weeks. Adjust dose by smoking level. NICE NG92.

options.label: Varenicline
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Varenicline 500 mcg OD 3 days, then 1 mg bd 12 weeks. Start 1–2 weeks before quit date. NICE NG92.

options.label: Bupropion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Bupropion 150 mg OD 6 days then 150 mg bd 7–9 weeks. Contraindicated in seizure, eating disorder. NICE NG92.

options.label: Non-drug (Child/Adult)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Psychoeducation for patient/parents. Environmental tweaks (school/work). Support groups. Consider CBT for adults. NICE NG87.

options.label: Drug treatment – Child (5+)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
First-line: Methylphenidate (titrate carefully, monitor height/weight/pulse/BP). Second-line: Lisdexamfetamine. Third-line: Atomoxetine or Guanfacine. Specialist initiation and shared care only. NICE NG87.

options.label: Drug treatment – Adult
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
First-line: Methylphenidate or Lisdexamfetamine. Second-line: Atomoxetine. Monitor BP/pulse. Specialist review required for initiation. NICE NG87.

options.label: Physical monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Pulse and BP (pre-titration then 6-monthly). Weight/height (6-monthly). Monitor for side effects (sleep, appetite, mood). NICE NG87.

options.label: Annual review
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Review effectiveness and need for continuing medication once a year. Assess for comorbidities (anxiety, depression). NICE NG87.

options.label: Suspected Dementia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History: Focused history (onset, progression, impact). Use 6-CIT or GPCOG screen.
2. Bloods: FBC, U&E, LFT, Bone, TFT, B12/Folate, HbA1c (exclude reversible causes).
3. Referral: Refer to Memory Clinic for formal diagnosis and imaging. NICE NG97.

options.label: Alzheimer's (Mild to Moderate)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cholinesterase Inhibitors: Donepezil, Rivastigmine, or Galantamine.
2. Warning: Check ECG for heart block / bradycardia before starting DONEPEZIL. NICE NG97.

options.label: Alzheimer's (Severe) / Contraindications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Memantine: 1st-line for severe Alzheimer's or if ChE inhibitors not tolerated. NICE NG97.

options.label: Mild (Croupy cough, no stridor at rest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Steroid: Single dose of Dexamethasone 0.15mg/kg oral (or Prednisolone 1mg/kg).
2. Advice: Usually self-limiting within 48h. Comfort child. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate / Severe (Stridor at rest, recession)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Do not examine throat (risk of epiglottitis).
2. Referral: Urgent hospital admission. Avoid distress. NICE CKS.

options.label: Safe for Home
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hydration: Ensure ≥ 50% normal fluid intake. Check wet nappies.
2. No Meds: Do not use inhalers, steroids, or antibiotics for bronchiolitis.
3. Safety-net: Return if RR > 60, grunting, or reduced feeding. NICE NG9.

options.label: Refer to Hospital
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: RR > 70, saturations < 92%, apnoeas, or persistent reduced feeding (<50%).
2. Action: Urgent Paediatric referral. NICE NG9.

options.label: Green (Low Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (Intermediate Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (High Risk / Sepsis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

options.label: Low Risk (Green)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting and follow-up. Provide written instructions on when to seek help. NICE NG51.

options.label: High Risk (Amber/Red)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
999 Ambulance. NEWS2 score calculation. ABCDE assessment. O2 to target 94-98%. IV access. Pre-hospital antibiotics if >1h from hospital. NICE NG51.

options.label: IM Adrenaline (999)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Adrenaline 1:1000 IM (anterolateral mid-thigh). Adult: 500mcg (0.5ml). Child 6-12: 300mcg. Child <6: 150mcg. Repeat every 5 mins if no improvement. High-flow O2. NICE NG193.

options.label: Child/Young Person
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to local multi-agency ASD pathway (Paediatrics/CAMHS). Review for co-occurring ADHD/LD. NICE CG128.

options.label: Adult suspected ASD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer for specialist diagnostic assessment if significant impact on social/working life. Use AQ-10 screening tool. NICE CG142.

options.label: Mild/Moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lid hygiene (warm compresses). Preservative-free lubricants (e.g. Hylo-Forte, Viscotears). Ointment at night (e.g. Lacri-Lube). NICE CKS Dry Eye.

options.label: Severe or refractory
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to Ophthalmology. Consider punctal plugs or ciclosporin drops. Exclude Sjogren's syndrome (check ANA, Ro/La).

options.label: Newly diagnosed/Suspected
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to secondary care for diagnosis and treatment initiation. First-line usually Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. Latanoprost). NICE NG81.

options.label: Community Monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check IOP, visual fields, and adherence. Beta-blockers (e.g. Timolol) used as adjunctive; check for contraindications (Asthma/Heart Block).

options.label: Bacterial Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds. Fusidic acid if pregnant. Safety-net for pain/vision loss. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected Corneal Ulcer/Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contact lens wearer? Painful? Fluorescein staining positive? Emergency Ophthalmology referral (same day). Avoid steroids.

options.label: Scleritis (Deep pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Deep, boring eye pain. Systemic associations (rheumatoid). Urgent Ophthalmology referral (within 24-48h). NICE CKS.

options.label: Sudden painless loss of vision (RAO)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Suspected Retinal Artery Occlusion. Emergency (999 or Eye Casualty). Stroke symptoms? TIA workup needed.

options.label: Painful red eye + nausea (Acute Glaucoma)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency referral. Fixed semi-dilated pupil. Give Acetazolamide 500mg IV/PO if remote from hospital (per local policy).

options.label: Floaters and flashes (Detachment)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Retinal detachment until proven otherwise. Urgent (same day) Ophthalmology review.

options.label: First-line (Drops)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Olive oil drops 2-3 times daily for 2 weeks. Avoid cotton buds. Sodium bicarbonate drops if oil fails. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mechanical removal
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Electronic irrigation or microsuction if drops fail and no perforation/recent surgery. Check for history of ear infections.

options.label: Acute Mastoiditis suspected
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency admission (Paediatrics/ENT). Post-auricular swelling/fluctuance, displaced pinna. IV antibiotics + imaging. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tenderness only (no swelling)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Careful review for media/externa. Urgent ENT opinion if clinical concern despite lack of classic signs. Safety-net strictly.

options.label: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Emergency (ENT same day). High-dose oral Prednisolone (e.g. 60mg OD for 7 days) started immediately. Urgent Audiogram. NICE NG98.

options.label: Unilateral Pulsatile Tinnitus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Urgent ENT referral for imaging (exclude glomus tumour/vascular malformation). Routine referral if non-pulsatile but persistent/distressing. NICE NG155.

options.label: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Valsalva manoeuvre. Nasal steroid spray (e.g. Fluticasone) for 4-6 weeks if obstructive. Decongestants (short-term only). NICE CKS.

options.label: Acute Pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Follow WHO pain ladder: Step 1 Paracetamol/NSAIDs; Step 2 Weak opioids (Codeine); Step 3 Strong opioids (Morphine). Non-drug: RICE for trauma. NICE CKS.

options.label: Chronic Pain (Primary)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Focus on function and quality of life. Offer supervised exercise, CBT, or acupuncture. Antidepressants (Duloxetine/Amitriptyline) for chronic primary pain. Avoid opioids. NICE NG193.

options.label: Shoulder
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Look (asymmetry, wasting); Feel (ACJ, SCJ, humerus); Move (Active/Passive: Abd, Flex, Rot). Tests: Hawkins-Kennedy (impingement), Empty Can (Supraspinatus).

options.label: Knee
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Look (effusion, alignment); Feel (joint line tenderness, temperature); Move (Active/Passive Flex/Ext). Tests: Lachman (ACL), McMurray (Meniscus), Patellar Tap (effusion).

options.label: Hip
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Look (gait, Trendelenburg); Feel (greater trochanter); Move (Flex, Int/Ext Rotation). Special: Thomas test (flexion contracture).

options.label: Spine (Back/Neck)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Look (curvature, scoliosis); Feel (spinous processes, paravertebral muscles); Move (Flex, Ext, Lat Flex). Neurology: SLR (Root stretch), Dermatomes, Myotomes, Reflexes.

options.label: Osteoarthritis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Diagnosis: Age ≥45, activity-related joint pain, no/brief morning stiffness (<30m). Management: Exercise, weight loss, topical NSAIDs, education. NICE NG226.

options.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis (Suspected)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Suspect if persistent joint synovitis (swelling). Urgent referral (within 3 weeks). Baseline: FBC, CRP, ESR, RF, Anti-CCP, X-rays. Start DMARD only after specialist review. NICE NG100.

options.label: Red Flags (Cauda Equina / Malignancy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral sciatica, night pain, weight loss, history of cancer. Urgent same-day referral/A&E. NICE NG59.

options.label: Stable / Spondylosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Keep active. NSAIDs (regular) for flare. Physiotherapy referral. Avoid imaging in non-specific low back pain. Reassure if no neurology. NICE NG59.

options.label: Mild (Sensory only)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Nocturnal splints (6 weeks). Steroid injection if no response. Nerve conduction studies if diagnosis uncertain. NICE CKS.

options.label: Severe (Motor / Wasting)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Thenar wasting or weakness → Urgent referral for surgical decompression. Review for systemic causes (Thyroid, Diabetes, Pregnancy).

options.label: Initial Screening
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
History: Sleep, stress, diet, drugs. Bloods: FBC, Ferritin, U&E, TFT, HbA1c, Vit D, Bone, LFT, Coeliac screen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected ME/CFS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Persistent fatigue >3 months. Check NICE NG206 for diagnostic criteria. Do not offer LET or GET. Focus on energy management (pacing).

options.label: Diagnosis (Age >45)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Perimenopause based on vasomotor symptoms and irregular periods. Menopause based on no periods for 1 year. No FSH needed. NICE NG23.

options.label: HRT Choice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Uterus present? Combined HRT (Cyclical if <1yr amenorrhoea, Continuous if >1yr). No Uterus? Oestrogen only. Start low dose. Review at 3m. NICE NG23.

options.label: Combined (CHC)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check UKMEC: BP, BMI, Migraine with aura, VTE risk, Smoking (>35). 7-day rule for missed pills. FSRH Guideline.

options.label: LARC (Implant/IUS/IUD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Most effective methods. Discuss Nexplanon (3y), Mirena (8y/HRT), Copper IUD. Follow FSRH LARC standards.

options.label: Lifestyle & BMI assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Calculate BMI and waist circumference. Set 5-10% weight loss goal. Tier 2 weight management referral. NICE CG189.

options.label: Pharmacotherapy (Orlistat/GLP-1)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Orlistat if BMI ≥30 (or ≥28 with comorbidities). GLP-1 (e.g. Semaglutide) via Tier 3/4 specialist clinics if BMI ≥35 (or ≥30 with comorb in some cases). NICE TA664.

options.label: Dry Eyes / Blepharitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lid hygiene (warm compresses, massage). Preservative-free artificial tears (e.g. Hypromellose, Carmellose). Review work environment / screen use. NICE CKS.

options.label: Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Viral/Allergic: cool compresses, lubricants. Bacterial: Topical antibiotic (Chloramphenicol 0.5%) if severe/persistent. Safety-net for 'red eye' warning signs. NICE CKS.

options.label: Glaucoma (Chronic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Prostaglandin analogues (e.g. Latanoprost) first-line. Monitor IOP and visual fields annually. Urgent referral if Acute Angle Closure suspected. NICE NG81.

options.label: No Red Flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Proceed to conservative or medical management. NICE NG12.

options.label: URGENT 2WW Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dysphagia (any age).
2. Unintentional weight loss + dyspepsia (≥55y).
3. Upper abdominal mass. NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 1: Lifestyle & Antacids
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Weight loss; stop smoking; avoid meal-to-bed gap (<3h).
2. Raise head of bed. Avoid triggers (coffee, spice, alcohol). NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 2: Full-dose PPI
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Omeprazole 20mg or Lansoprazole 30mg OD for 1 month.
2. Review: If symptoms controlled, reduce to 'as needed' low dose. NICE NG12.

options.label: Step 3: H. pylori Testing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Test if dyspepsia persistent despite PPI (ensure off PPI for 2 weeks before test).
2. If Urea Breath Test / Stool Antigen positive: Eradication therapy. NICE NG12.

options.label: Clinical Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Vitals (NEWS2 if unwell), targeted history, and examination. Exclude red flags. Review trend vs previous presentations. Use shared decision making.

options.label: Safety-netting
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Provide clear 'When to contact' triggers: worsening pain, fever >38.5C, respiratory distress, or new neurological signs. Document patient understanding.

options.label: Follow-up Plan
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Review in 1-4 weeks depending on severity. Consider baseline bloods (FBC/CRP) if symptoms persist. Patient information leaflet/link provided.
